nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code for a partial recursive function and let $n$ be its number in the standard encoding of codes as natural numbers. For a binary string $w$, the description of $c$ running on $w$ is the binary string $1^n 0 w$, that is, $n$ ones, then a zero, then $w$.
nodes.title: Description of a code running on an input

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a partial recursive function from binary strings to binary strings, viewed as a description method. Then there is a natural number $c$ such that for all binary strings $x$ and $p$ for which $D(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ satisfies $K(x) \le |p| + c$, where $|p|$ is the length of $p$.
nodes.title: Optimality (the invariance theorem)

nodes.summary: For every binary string $x$ there is a binary string $p$ whose length is the Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ and such that $U(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, where $U$ is the universal description method.
nodes.title: Shortest descriptions exist

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a partial recursive function from binary strings to binary strings. Then there is a code $c$ for a partial recursive function such that running $c$ equals $D$ as a partial function: for every binary string $w$, running $c$ on $w$ is defined exactly when $D(w)$ is, and then has the same value.
nodes.title: Every partial recursive description method has a code
Incompressible strings, and Kolmogorov complexity is not computable

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $c$ such that for all binary strings $x$ and $y$, the Kolmogorov complexity of their concatenation $xy$ satisfies $K(xy) \le 2K(x) + K(y) + c$.
nodes.title: Concatenation costs at most twice the first part

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $c$ such that for every binary string $x$, the Kolmogorov complexity of the concatenation $xx$ of $x$ with itself satisfies $K(xx) \le K(x) + c$.
nodes.title: Doubling costs a constant

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $c$ such that every binary string $x$ satisfies $K(x) \le |x| + c$, where $K(x)$ is the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ and $|x|$ is its length.
nodes.title: Complexity is at most the length plus a constant

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $p$ be binary strings such that $U(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, where $U$ is the universal description method. Then the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ is at most the length of $p$: $K(x) \le |p|$.
nodes.title: A description bounds the complexity

nodes.summary: The Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ of a binary string $x$ is the least length of a binary string $p$ such that $U(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, where $U$ is the universal description method.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov complexity

nodes.summary: For binary strings $p$ and $q$, the pair description of $p$ and $q$ is the binary string $1^{|p|} 0 p q$, that is, $|p|$ ones, where $|p|$ is the length of $p$, then a zero, then $p$, then $q$.
nodes.title: Pair description

nodes.summary: Write a binary string $s$ as $1^n s'$, where $n$ is the number of leading $1$s, and let $r$ be $s'$ without its first letter ($r$ is empty when $s'$ is). Let $r_1$ be the first $\min(n, |r|)$ letters of $r$ and $r_2$ the remaining ones. The pair reader maps $s$ to the concatenation $U(r_1)\,U(r_2)$, where $U$ is the universal description method, and is undefined when $U(r_1)$ or $U(r_2)$ is undefined. On a pair…
nodes.title: Reading pair descriptions

nodes.summary: The universal description method, as a partial function from binary strings to binary strings, is partial recursive.
nodes.title: The universal description method is partial recursive

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ of a partial recursive function on the natural numbers and a binary string $w$, running $c$ on $w$ evaluates $c$ at the number encoding $w$; if this halts with output $m$, the result is the binary string encoded by $m$. The result is undefined when the evaluation does not halt or $m$ encodes no binary string.
nodes.title: Running a program on a binary string

nodes.summary: A description `1ⁿ 0 w` runs code number `n` on `w`; a string of `1`s describes nothing.
nodes.title: The universal description method
Upper semicomputability of Kolmogorov complexity, and incompressible strings

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
